Irene — quick take after reviewing Novum's comments.

- Section 4.2 (onward transfers): propose we accept the principle of a two-tier fallback if we add explicit language that: (i) Redwood may route to a compatible variant in the event of capacity constraints, and (ii) any onward transfer requires either SCCs or an approved transfer addendum signed by both parties. Suggested redline attached.
- Training telemetry: we should accept a narrowly scoped aggregation carveout limited to non-personalized telemetry and include a 90-day retention cap plus a right for Novum to request deletion of identified artifacts.
- Subprocessor list: recommend we provide a live subprocessor page (link) and an archive export as evidence; ops needs 5 business days to generate the archive for the initial handover.

Attachment: redline_comments.pdf (pdf)

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Claire Park <claire.park@novumhealth.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Sep 2026 15:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft DPA and SCCs — proposed path forward

Claire / Irene / Ben — thanks for the notes. From legal's side we've reviewed Novum's redline and Ben's suggestions. Proposed path forward: 

1) SCCs vs transfer addendum: Redwood can accept a two-tier approach provided the transfer addendum explicitly references the SCCs and contains an explicit fallback waterfall (SCCs -> transfer addendum -> compatible variant fallback). This keeps contract clarity and allows operational routing.

2) Training telemetry carveout: legal will accept a narrowly tailored clause limited to:
   - Aggregated, pseudonymized telemetry only;
   - No retention beyond 90 days unless mutually agreed;
   - Scope limited to optimization of caching and batching;
   - Novum retains the right to request deletion of any artifacts tied to their account.

3) Evidence and ops handoff: attached is our standard Evidence_Instructions.pdf and a draft responses doc. Ops can produce a subprocessor export and KMS key-usage summary within 5 business days after countersignature. For audit logs (token-level latency/cost traces) we will provide a redacted extract; full logs require an SIR with specific scope.

Next steps / timeline: Jordan (Legal) will incorporate the agreed language into Redwood_Responses_to_Novum_Redline.docx and send a consolidated comment set by EOD Mon 21 Sep. After Novum confirms, procurement will finalize order form edits and route for signatures (target: 24 Sep).

Attachments: Redwood_Responses_to_Novum_Redline.docx (docx), Evidence_Instructions.pdf (pdf)

Regards,
Jordan Blake
Senior Counsel, Contracts
